skills.name: abstract-title
skills.description: Create concise titles and abstracts whose claims match the actual study and results. Use when a researcher needs write evidence-aligned titles and abstracts.

skills.name: ai-use-disclosure
skills.description: Create a disclosure grounded in a real record of tools, tasks, and human verification. Use when a researcher needs document generative-ai use transparently.

skills.name: anti-defensive-writing
skills.description: Remove needless apology, hedging, and process narration while keeping all real limitations and unfavorable findings intact. Use when a researcher needs revise academic prose to be confident without concealing evidence.

skills.name: citation-verification
skills.description: Check whether bibliographic records resolve and whether in-text claims are supported by the cited source. Use when a researcher needs verify references and doi metadata.

skills.name: claim-evidence-audit
skills.description: Catch overclaiming, missing evidence, scope drift, and unsupported causal language. Use when a researcher needs audit every substantive claim against evidence.

skills.name: critical-paper-reading
skills.description: Produce a structured reading note grounded in the paper's actual text, tables, and figures. Use when a researcher needs read a paper critically and trace claims to the source.

skills.name: data-extraction-review
skills.description: Populate a review extraction sheet and validate comparability before synthesis. Use when a researcher needs extract study characteristics and outcomes consistently.

skills.name: data-management
skills.description: Define how research data are collected, documented, stored, shared, preserved, and deleted. Use when a researcher needs create a research data-management plan.

skills.name: evidence-extraction
skills.description: Convert a defined set of papers into traceable, comparable evidence records. Use when a researcher needs extract comparable evidence into a structured table.

skills.name: experiment-design
skills.description: Design experiments that isolate mechanisms and test claims rather than accumulate metrics. Use when a researcher needs plan controlled experiments and ablations.

skills.name: figure-table-audit
skills.description: Check whether exhibits are interpretable, internally consistent, and aligned with manuscript claims. Use when a researcher needs audit figures, tables, captions, and quantitative consistency.

skills.name: grant-proposal
skills.description: Connect significance, innovation, approach, feasibility, and expected outputs to credible evidence. Use when a researcher needs develop a fundable, evidence-based research proposal.

skills.name: journal-fit
skills.description: Compare candidate venues against scope, audience, article type, quality signals, and current author instructions. Use when a researcher needs assess journal and venue fit using verifiable criteria.

skills.name: literature-discovery
skills.description: Use scholarly metadata services to discover candidate papers and keep provenance attached to every record. Use when a researcher needs discover and deduplicate scholarly records.

skills.name: literature-synthesis
skills.description: Build an analytical synthesis of agreements, disagreements, mechanisms, and unresolved questions. Use when a researcher needs synthesize literature by evidence pattern, not paper-by-paper summary.

skills.name: methods-writing
skills.description: Turn study records into a transparent methods section with traceable procedural detail. Use when a researcher needs draft methods with enough detail to reproduce.

skills.name: ml-evaluation-audit
skills.description: Check whether model comparisons and reported metrics support the stated ML claims. Use when a researcher needs audit machine-learning evaluation design.

skills.name: novelty-gap-mapping
skills.description: Identify evidence-supported gaps and differentiate a true open question from a search failure. Use when a researcher needs map candidate research gaps without novelty inflation.

skills.name: paper-triage
skills.description: Prioritize a paper queue transparently without treating metadata ranking as scientific appraisal. Use when a researcher needs triage papers for relevance and reading priority.

skills.name: peer-review
skills.description: Provide a structured, evidence-based review focused on validity, contribution, and clarity. Use when a researcher needs review a manuscript as a critical but constructive referee.

skills.name: prisma-reporting
skills.description: Audit the arithmetic and documentation of evidence-selection stages before reporting them. Use when a researcher needs reconcile review flow counts and reporting completeness.

skills.name: rebuttal-letter
skills.description: Draft a calm, auditable response linked to real manuscript changes and new evidence. Use when a researcher needs prepare a point-by-point response to peer reviewers.

skills.name: related-work-writing
skills.description: Organize prior work around conceptual and methodological distinctions that motivate the present study. Use when a researcher needs write a critical related-work section.

skills.name: reproducibility-audit
skills.description: Determine whether another researcher has enough information to rerun the analysis. Use when a researcher needs audit computational reproducibility.

skills.name: research-code-review
skills.description: Inspect code paths that affect data, models, metrics, and reported conclusions. Use when a researcher needs review research code for correctness and scientific traceability.

skills.name: research-design
skills.description: Match the design to the question, estimand, constraints, and threats to validity. Use when a researcher needs choose and audit a study design.

skills.name: research-ethics
skills.description: Surface issues requiring formal ethics, biosafety, data-protection, authorship, or institutional review. Use when a researcher needs identify research ethics and integrity questions early.

skills.name: research-presentation
skills.description: Design a talk for a defined audience and time rather than compressing every paragraph into slides. Use when a researcher needs turn a paper into a clear research talk.

skills.name: research-question-framing
skills.description: Turn a broad interest into a precise, answerable question with scope, constructs, population/context, and success criteria. Use when a researcher needs frame a tractable research question.

skills.name: researchforge-abstract-and-title
skills.description: Create accurate, informative paper titles and abstracts that expose the question, method, strongest verified result, scope, and contribution within the venue word limit.

skills.name: researchforge-anti-defensive-writing
skills.description: Revise academic prose to remove unnecessary apology, self-undermining, defensive repetition, and weak organization while preserving negative findings, uncertainty, limitations, and all material evidence. Use for abstracts, introductions, results, discussions, conclusions, and rebuttals.

skills.name: researchforge-bibtex-hygiene
skills.description: Clean and normalize BibTeX libraries, identify duplicate or malformed entries, standardize DOI and URL fields, and preserve citation-key stability.

skills.name: researchforge-citation-verification
skills.description: Check DOI and bibliographic metadata against authoritative registries, detect mismatches and unresolved references, and produce a citation audit. Use before submission or when a bibliography may contain hallucinated citations.

skills.name: researchforge-conference-submission-preflight
skills.description: Audit a manuscript and artifacts against a target conference or journal’s current author instructions, formatting rules, anonymization, ethics, and submission requirements.

skills.name: researchforge-dataset-audit
skills.description: Audit a research dataset for provenance, license, schema, missingness, duplicates, leakage, split integrity, class imbalance, and sensitive-data risk.

skills.name: researchforge-deep-paper-reading
skills.description: Read a research paper critically and extract its question, contribution, method, evidence, assumptions, limitations, and reproducibility details with page-level traceability.

skills.name: researchforge-error-analysis
skills.description: Turn model failures and unexpected results into a structured error taxonomy, representative cases, root-cause hypotheses, and targeted follow-up experiments.

skills.name: researchforge-evidence-matrix-synthesis
skills.description: Synthesize a paper corpus into a traceable evidence matrix, thematic map, agreement/disagreement analysis, and carefully qualified narrative synthesis.

skills.name: researchforge-experimental-design
skills.description: Design controlled, feasible experiments with valid comparators, randomization, measurement plans, sample-size reasoning, and threats-to-validity controls.

skills.name: researchforge-hypothesis-generation
skills.description: Generate testable hypotheses from a literature map and mechanism model, including operational predictions, rival explanations, and falsification criteria.

skills.name: researchforge-literature-search-strategy
skills.description: Design reproducible searches across scholarly databases, produce exact query strings and a search log, and use backward/forward citation chasing. Use for related work, scoping reviews, systematic reviews, or novelty checks.

skills.name: researchforge-llm-evaluation-design
skills.description: Design robust evaluations for language models and agents, including task construction, benchmark contamination checks, human review, graders, uncertainty, and failure analysis.

skills.name: researchforge-ml-experiment-planning
skills.description: Plan compute-aware machine-learning experiments with credible baselines, fair comparisons, ablations, seeds, data splits, and decision rules.

skills.name: researchforge-paper-triage
skills.description: Screen paper titles and abstracts against predeclared criteria, deduplicate candidate records, and keep an auditable inclusion/exclusion log. Use when a literature search returns more papers than can be read in full.

skills.name: researchforge-peer-review
skills.description: Produce a fair, evidence-based peer review that evaluates contribution, method, evidence, clarity, ethics, and reproducibility with actionable major and minor comments.

skills.name: researchforge-rebuttal-and-response
skills.description: Prepare point-by-point author responses to peer review, distinguishing clarifications, corrections, new analyses, and disagreements with supporting evidence.

skills.name: researchforge-reproducibility-audit
skills.description: Audit whether a computational research result can be rerun from available code, data provenance, environment, configuration, seeds, and documented commands.

skills.name: researchforge-research-code-review
skills.description: Review research code for scientific validity, evaluation leakage, implementation bugs, determinism, numerical correctness, security, and maintainability.

skills.name: researchforge-research-decision-gate
skills.description: Evaluate whether a research idea or experiment should proceed, be narrowed, be redesigned, or be stopped using scientific value, evidence, feasibility, and resource constraints.

skills.name: researchforge-research-ethics-and-data-governance
skills.description: Review research plans for consent, privacy, data rights, institutional approval, risk minimization, security, and responsible release of datasets and models.

skills.name: researchforge-research-gap-analysis
skills.description: Identify meaningful empirical, methodological, measurement, theoretical, contextual, or reproducibility gaps from an evidence corpus and prioritize researchable opportunities.

skills.name: researchforge-research-grant-writing
skills.description: Develop evidence-grounded research grant proposals with a clear problem, aims, methodology, milestones, risk management, impact, and defensible budget narrative.

skills.name: researchforge-research-question-framing
skills.description: Turn a broad interest into a specific, answerable research question, a defensible scope, operational definitions, and measurable outcomes. Use before literature searches, proposals, theses, or experiments.

skills.name: researchforge-results-to-claims
skills.description: Map every manuscript claim to the evidence that supports it, evaluate scope and uncertainty, and rewrite overbroad conclusions into defensible statements.

skills.name: researchforge-scientific-visualization
skills.description: Choose and produce scientific figures that communicate the measured result accurately, with appropriate scales, uncertainty, labels, annotations, and reproducible source data.

skills.name: researchforge-scientific-writing
skills.description: Draft and revise research manuscripts from verified evidence, with a clear argument, section-level purpose, consistent terminology, and appropriate scholarly tone.

skills.name: researchforge-statistical-analysis-plan
skills.description: Choose and document statistical analyses, estimands, assumptions, uncertainty estimates, multiplicity handling, and missing-data procedures before outcome inspection.

skills.name: researchforge-systematic-review
skills.description: Plan and execute a transparent systematic or scoping review using a protocol, reproducible searches, explicit screening, structured extraction, and appropriate PRISMA reporting.

skills.name: researchforge-thesis-roadmap
skills.description: Turn a thesis or dissertation topic into a scoped research plan with chapter logic, literature milestones, methods, deliverables, risks, and review gates.

skills.name: results-discussion-writing
skills.description: Separate observed results from interpretation and connect each finding to its uncertainty and context. Use when a researcher needs write results and discussion without interpretation drift.

skills.name: search-strategy-design
skills.description: Create database-specific search strings and a search log that another researcher can rerun. Use when a researcher needs design a reproducible literature search.

skills.name: statistics-audit
skills.description: Find common statistical inconsistencies and improve clarity without replacing a qualified statistician. Use when a researcher needs audit statistical reasoning and reported numbers.

skills.name: study-screening
skills.description: Apply prespecified inclusion/exclusion criteria and document reasons for decisions. Use when a researcher needs screen records against explicit eligibility criteria.

skills.name: systematic-review-protocol
skills.description: Specify the review before screening to reduce hindsight-driven decisions. Use when a researcher needs draft a transparent systematic-review protocol.
